results.requirement: Server-to-server access uses an account-scoped API key with no per-user consent, impersonation or domain claim.
results.evidence: src/server/auth.ts authenticate() accepts "Authorization: Bearer tsk_...", looks the SHA-256 up in api_keys and needs no consent screen, token exchange or domain claim; keys are made in src/server/routes-account.ts (POST /api-keys). Proven by tests/flow.test.ts 'accounts are isolated, API keys work, members see only their own envelopes' and my run of tests/out/audit-developer/api.ts (key used seconds after sign-up, first call 200).
results.gap: The key belongs to the person who made it, not to the account. It acts with that person's role and sight (a member's key lists only that member's envelopes), admins cannot see or revoke other people's keys (GET /api-keys filters on user_id), and removing that person from the team deletes their keys without a word (checked: the integration then gets 401 "Please sign in.", no email was sent). Keys also carry the full role with no narrower permission: an owner's key can invite a new admin and mint more keys (checked). The scheme is matched case-sensitively: "bearer tsk_..." is refused with "Please sign in."
results.suggested_fix: src/server/auth.ts and routes-account.ts: add account-level keys that an admin creates with a chosen permission (for example send-only, read-only, admin) and that survive a member leaving; show admins every key on the account with who made it and when it was last used; in DELETE /account/members/:id hand the leaver's keys to the successor or name them in the removal dialog and email the admins; match the Bearer scheme without regard to case.

results.requirement: There is one API hostname for all accounts; no separate base-URL discovery call is needed before the first request.
results.evidence: Every route is served under /api on the one host by src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts and src/server/router.ts handle(); src/server/openapi.ts publishes a single server entry and no route returns a region or base address (listRoutes()). tests/flow.test.ts 'accounts are isolated, API keys work...' makes GET /envelopes the very first call with a new key and gets 200; my api.ts run did the same.

results.requirement: Test mode is a key type on the same account and host, so templates, settings and webhooks carry over and going live means swapping one key.
results.evidence: There is only one environment, so nothing has to be carried over and there is no key to swap: the same key, account, templates and webhooks are used from the first call (api.ts). The Settings screen and src/server/openapi.ts say so in words: "no separate test environment".
results.gap: There is no test key type at all, so every call a developer makes while building is live: real emails go to the recipients, a signature is held and used whenever the signer is someone else (a free account is refused on its 4th send with 402, a GROWalition account on its 13th; both checked), the envelopes count in reports and the public impact totals, and the certificate looks like a real one. The column envelopes.test_mode is created in src/server/db.ts but nothing reads or writes it. The only free way to practise is to send documents to yourself.
results.suggested_fix: Add a key type tsk_test_... (api_keys.mode) in routes-account.ts; have auth.ts mark the request as test and createEnvelope() set envelopes.test_mode=1. For test envelopes: deliver emails only to the key owner's own address, hold and use no signatures (credits.needed() returns 0), stamp "TEST" on pages and certificate in pdf.ts, leave them out of /reports/summary and /public/impact, and add "test": true to webhook bodies. Same host, templates, settings and webhooks.

results.requirement: A refused call returns the exact missing permission and a link to the screen that fixes it; a wrong-environment key returns its own specific error.
results.evidence: Every refusal is JSON with a sentence and a request_id (src/server/router.ts handle(); tests/flow.test.ts 'retries are safe and every answer can be traced'). Checked in api.ts: admin-only route with a member key gives 403 "Only account admins can do that."; out of signatures gives 402 with how many are needed, how many are left and the price; unconfirmed email gives 403 that says to confirm it. There is one environment, so a wrong-environment key cannot exist.
results.gap: No refusal carries a link, and there is no machine-readable code or permission name. Every key problem gets the same 401 "Please sign in.": no header, lower-case "bearer", a malformed key, an unknown key, a revoked key and a key whose owner was removed (all checked). That is wrong advice for a program and gives no hint which of the six it was.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/router.ts handle(): when an Authorization header is present but no key matches, answer 401 with code "api_key_invalid" and "This API key is not recognised. It may have been revoked, or the person who made it has left the team. Create a new one at <baseUrl>/app/settings?tab=developers". Give HttpError (src/server/util.ts) optional code and fix_url fields and set them for 401, 402 (Plan page), 403 admin-only (Team page), 403 unconfirmed email and 403 paused; add both to the Error schema in openapi.ts.

results.requirement: Any SDK that uses expiring tokens refreshes them automatically before expiry.
results.evidence: No SDK is published and nothing expires: API keys have no expiry column (src/server/db.ts api_keys) and authenticate() never rejects a key for age, so there is no token to refresh.

results.requirement: API access, webhooks and embedded signing are included in every paid plan under the same document allowance, with a public per-document rate.
results.evidence: No plan check exists on POST /api-keys or POST /webhooks (src/server/routes-account.ts) or on POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view (routes-envelopes.ts); API sends go through the same sendEnvelope() and the same signature ledger (src/server/credits.ts) as the app, at the one rate in src/lib/impact.ts PRICING. Checked with billing counted: free account (api.ts, hooks.ts) made a key, got 4 webhook events delivered, got an embedded link, sent 3 envelopes and was refused the 4th with 402 quoting "$9 for 9 signatures"; an account that entered GROWalition, typed in lower case (code.ts), got the plan free, 12 signatures, webhook and embedded link, and the 13th send was refused quoting "$1 a signature". The payments table stayed empty in both runs. tests/billing.test.ts 'the code GROWalition makes the monthly plan free' covers the code itself.
results.gap: The price is stated in the 402 answer but not in the API description (openapi.ts); the public pages that carry it are being rewritten and were not judged.
results.suggested_fix: Add the two prices from PRICING to info.description in src/server/openapi.ts so the rate is in the machine-readable description too.

results.requirement: A free sandbox issues keys instantly and has documented limits; a limited or held call returns the reason.
results.evidence: A free account gets a working key at once, even before its email is confirmed (api.ts). Held calls say why (envelopes.ts sendEnvelope()): 402 with needed/left/price, 403 "Confirm your email address before you send...", 429 "New accounts can send to 50 people a day during their first week..." (code.ts), 422 for a fake payment notice (tests/trust.test.ts 'new free accounts cannot send fake payment notices...'). A refused create-and-send leaves no stray draft (checked).
results.gap: It is not a sandbox: sends from it are live (see the test-mode requirement). The limits are not written down where a developer reads: src/server/openapi.ts mentions only the 402, 25 MB / 500 pages and 500 bulk rows. Missing are the 3 welcome signatures, the 50-people-a-day cap in the first week (it also applies to GROWalition accounts), email confirmation before sending, the payment-notice screen, and 30 documents / 50 recipients / 2,000 fields per envelope. A 429 carries no Retry-After.
results.suggested_fix: Add a "Limits" part to info.description in src/server/openapi.ts built from PRICING and src/lib/policy.ts so the numbers cannot drift, document the 402/403/422/429 answers on POST /envelopes and POST /envelopes/{id}/send, and send Retry-After with 429 from router.ts.

results.requirement: Going live is self-serve with no sales conversation or manual review for standard use.
results.evidence: A key has no pending or review state: api_keys has no status column and authenticate() checks only the hash and team membership (src/server/auth.ts). In api.ts a brand-new account confirmed its email, made a key and sent an envelope through it within the same second. Paying is self-serve checkout, proven against a simulated provider in tests/billing.test.ts ('the monthly plan: $9 adds 9 signatures...', 'top-ups: $1 a signature...', 'the code GROWalition makes the monthly plan free').
results.gap: One hold is not self-serve: an unpaid account (free, or free through GROWalition) may send to 50 people a day in its first week, and the refusal only says "Contact support". The operator screen has no way to lift it for one account, and a GROWalition account cannot pay to lift it because checkout is refused for it.
results.suggested_fix: Add an operator action in src/server/routes-trust.ts that lifts the first-week cap for one account (accounts.sending_cleared_at) and check it in sendEnvelope().

results.requirement: API billing starts only once production access is active on the account.
results.evidence: There is no API plan and no API charge that could start early: API calls draw on the same signature balance as the app, and money only moves through a checkout the customer starts (src/server/routes-billing.ts). After 17 API send attempts across two accounts the payments table was empty (api.ts, code.ts).

results.requirement: SDK clients hold no shared mutable state; a CI test runs two tenants concurrently in one process and asserts no credential crossover.
results.evidence: Sign&Grow publishes no SDK, only the HTTP API and /api/openapi.json, so there is no client object that could share state between tenants.
results.gap: The same kind of defect does exist on the server: one process-wide value (the address of the latest request) is used in every tenant's emails. It is reported under bugs.
results.suggested_fix: See the first bug.

results.requirement: Every SDK release is gated on an end-to-end suite against the sandbox: get credentials, send a document, download the signed PDF and verify its checksum, receive a webhook.
results.evidence: No SDK exists, so I judged the API's own release check, npm test (61 of 61 pass, run today). tests/flow.test.ts 'full signing flow: order, access code, completion, certificate, verification' sends, signs, downloads and proves the file's SHA-256 through /public/verify; 'accounts are isolated, API keys work...' gets a key.
results.gap: No test touches src/server/webhooks.ts: nothing checks delivery, the signature header, the three tries, sending again or the failure email (searching the tests for "webhook" finds only the payment provider's). No test calls recipient-view. The key test only lists envelopes. Nothing runs the suite automatically: the repository's .github/workflows has no job for sign-and-grow. My throwaway hooks.ts shows the webhook leg works today, but a regression would not be caught.
results.suggested_fix: Add tests/api.test.ts that uses only an API key, with ALLOW_PRIVATE_WEBHOOKS=1 and a local http receiver: make a key, upload, create and send with an Idempotency-Key, sign, receive envelope.completed with a valid X-SignAndGrow-Signature, download, and assert the SHA-256 equals final_sha256. Add a CI job that runs npm test and npm run typecheck on every push to sign-and-grow/.

results.requirement: Create calls accept an idempotency key so a retried or timed-out call never sends a document twice.
results.evidence: POST /envelopes in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts reads Idempotency-Key and keeps it in idempotency_keys; tests/flow.test.ts 'retries are safe and every answer can be traced'. In api.ts a repeated call and two calls at the same instant both returned one envelope and one email; POST /envelopes/:id/send repeated gives 400 "already been sent" and one email.
results.gap: Three holes, all reproduced. (1) POST /bulk ignores the header: the same call twice made two batches and emailed every person twice. Bulk also runs inside the request, up to 500 sends each waiting on the mail server, which is exactly where a client times out and retries. (2) The key record is never cleaned up: create a draft with a key, delete it, then create-and-send with the same key and every retry makes and sends a new envelope (2 envelopes, 2 emails). (3) The key is looked up per account without checking who asks or what was sent: another team member using the same key got the first member's envelope back, and a different body is silently ignored.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/routes-envelopes.ts: honour the header on POST /bulk (store the batch id and return the first answer); store user_id and a hash of the body with each key, answer 409 when either differs, and run mine() on a replayed envelope; replace the stale row when its envelope is gone (INSERT OR REPLACE, or delete the row in DELETE /envelopes/:id); make bulk a queued job that returns the batch id at once.

results.requirement: SDKs use platform-default TLS verification with no off switch, keep runtime dependencies minimal, and ship a patched release within 7 days of a high-severity advisory.
results.evidence: No SDK is shipped, so there is no client TLS switch, client dependency tree or SDK release to patch. For the server's own outbound calls: webhook delivery uses plain fetch with default certificate checks and no switch to turn them off (src/server/webhooks.ts), and npm audit --omit=dev reported 0 vulnerabilities today.

results.requirement: Every SDK call has a default timeout of 30 seconds, a per-call override and cancellation, and errors carry HTTP status, error code, message and request ID.
results.evidence: No SDK, so timeouts and cancelling belong to the caller's HTTP client. Every API error is JSON with the HTTP status, a message and request_id, and X-Request-Id is on every response (src/server/router.ts handle(); tests/flow.test.ts 'retries are safe and every answer can be traced'; api.ts).
results.gap: There is no error code. A program has to match English sentences: 403 alone means "admins only", "confirm your email" or "sending is paused", and 400 has dozens of meanings. On the server side, POST /bulk and POST /envelopes with send:true hold the connection until every email has been handed to the mail server, with no time limit of our own (src/server/mail.ts uses the mail library's defaults, which run to minutes).
results.suggested_fix: Add a stable code to HttpError in src/server/util.ts and to the Error schema in src/server/openapi.ts (out_of_signatures, email_not_confirmed, sending_paused, admin_only, api_key_invalid, daily_limit ...); set connection and socket timeouts on the transport in mail.ts; queue bulk sends so the call returns straight away.

results.requirement: A signing link can be requested for any recipient by recipient ID and re-issued any number of times until the document is completed; editing a recipient's name or email does not invalidate it.
results.evidence: POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts returns the link for any recipient id once the envelope is sent, with no "embedded" flag needed. api.ts: links came back for the current signer, a later signer and a copy recipient; 25 repeat calls returned the identical address; a name fix kept the link working (also tests/trust.test.ts 'small things that stop people getting stuck'); the link is still issued after that person finished.
results.gap: Changing the email address (POST /correct or PUT) or the signer handing over to someone else replaces the link: the address already given out answers 410 (checked). The same recipient id does return the new one, but nothing tells the integration: no webhook fires for POST /correct or for a reassignment (corr.ts; envelope.corrected only fires from PUT). No link before sending (404 on a draft). Every request writes "Signing link issued" into the audit trail, which is printed on the certificate (28 requests gave 28 lines). The person is always emailed the same link as well; that cannot be turned off for someone signing inside another product. No test covers the endpoint.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/envelopes.ts: fire envelope.corrected with recipient_id and link_replaced: true from correctRecipient() and reassignRecipient(). routes-envelopes.ts: log "Signing link issued" once per recipient per day and keep it off the certificate; accept the call on drafts or say plainly to send first. Add a recipient option notify: false that skips the invitation email. Add a test.

results.requirement: The embed component fires completed, declined, closed, error and timeout events and removes itself from the page when the session ends.
results.evidence: There is on purpose no embed component, so nothing can be left covering the host page: next.config.mjs sends X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN on every path (header checked on /sign/<token>; a frame on another origin was blocked). Outcomes reach the integrator's server as webhooks: recipient.completed, envelope.declined, envelope.completed, envelope.expired (hooks.ts: delivered, signature valid).
results.gap: There is no way back to the integrator's product. The signing link takes no return address (opened with ?return_url=..., it was ignored) and the finished screen offers only View, Download, How we count and Help (looked at it in a browser). Nothing signals closed, error or session end. Webhook events have no test.
results.suggested_fix: Let recipient-view accept return_url, checked against a list of https origins the account sets once under Settings, API and webhooks, and store it on the recipient. In src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx show "Back to <host>" and go there with ?event=completed|declined|closed|expired|error&envelope_id=...&recipient_id=... after finishing, declining, a closed or expired envelope, and a failed load. Say in the API description that links do not time out.

results.requirement: Allowed origins are configured once per app; a misconfigured origin fails immediately with a readable console error.
results.evidence: Signing is never shown inside another site's page, so there is no origin list to get wrong: next.config.mjs refuses framing for every origin, and an attempt fails at once with the browser's own console line "Refused to display ... in a frame because it set 'X-Frame-Options' to 'sameorigin'" (seen in Chromium via ui.mjs). The API description says the page cannot be framed.

results.requirement: An embedded session token is scoped to one document and grants no access to the main web app.
results.evidence: The link is authorised only by recipients.token in src/server/routes-sign.ts find() and reaches only /sign/:token routes for that one recipient on that one envelope; the app accepts only a ts_session cookie or a tsk_ key (src/server/auth.ts authenticate()). Checked in api.ts: after opening the link and consenting, the browser held no cookies; /envelopes, the same envelope by id, /inbox, /api-keys, /webhooks, /billing, /contacts, /export, the sender's download and the source file all answered 401 and /me returned no user; the token could not read a document from another envelope (404). tests/flow.test.ts 'approver, viewer and in-person roles; documents stay private until it is your turn' covers the turn rule.

results.requirement: An integration health page shows, per connector, status, last successful sync and failed deliveries with a plain-language error and a retry button.
results.evidence: Settings, API and webhooks (src/app/app/settings/page.tsx Developers(), fed by GET /webhooks in src/server/routes-account.ts) lists each webhook, the latest deliveries as Delivered or Failed with the HTTP status, an error text, the time, and a "Send again" button (redeliver() in src/server/webhooks.ts); API keys show when they were last used. I looked at it with one working and two failing endpoints (tests/out/audit-developer/shot-developers2.png) and resent a delivery in hooks.ts.
results.gap: There is no health per webhook: no status, no last successful delivery, and a delivery row does not say which webhook or which envelope it was for (three webhooks gave three look-alike rows). Errors are raw: "fetch failed", or just "Failed (500)". Only the latest 30 rows across all webhooks are shown (45 failures in the log, 30 listed), with no paging and no "failed only". "Send again" is one row at a time and vanishes once the stored body is dropped (see bugs). No test.
results.suggested_fix: GET /webhooks: return for each webhook last_success_at, last_failure_at, failures in a row and a status (healthy or failing); accept ?webhook_id=, ?failed=1 and ?before= for paging. Screen: group deliveries under their webhook with a status badge and a link to the envelope, turn errors into sentences ("We could not connect to your server", "Your server took longer than 10 seconds", "Your address redirects; give us the final one", "Your server answered with an error (500)"), and add "Send all failed again".

results.requirement: The admin is emailed when a connector fails or a credential is about to expire.
results.evidence: src/server/webhooks.ts deliver(): after three failed deliveries in a row every owner and admin gets "A Sign&Grow webhook keeps failing" with the address, the reason and a link to the log, at most once a day. Checked in hooks.ts: nothing after one or two failures, one email after the third, none for the fourth the same day. Nothing expires: API keys and webhook secrets have no expiry.
results.gap: The one credential the software itself removes goes silently: taking a member off the team deletes their API keys with no email, and the removal dialog does not mention it (checked: the key answers 401, 0 emails). A delivery is only tried three times within about six seconds, so any outage longer than that needs a person to press "Send again" on each row; nothing is resent when the endpoint recovers and no email says it recovered. The alert has no test.
results.suggested_fix: routes-account.ts DELETE /account/members/:id and routes-trust.ts (closing an account): email admins the names of the keys that stop working, and say so in the dialog in settings/page.tsx. webhooks.ts: write the delivery row before the first try and keep retrying from the timer (src/server/cron.ts) with growing gaps for 24 hours; email once when a failing webhook delivers again. Add tests for both.

results.requirement: Outbound events are idempotent: a re-sync never re-sends a 'completed' notification.
results.evidence: fireWebhooks() in src/server/webhooks.ts gives each event an id that is reused on the automatic retries and on "Send again" (hooks.ts: the resent body was byte-for-byte the same, same id). completeEnvelope() in src/server/envelopes.ts runs once: one envelope.completed and one "Completed" email per address, even when two finish requests arrive together (hooks.ts, race.ts).
results.gap: The per-person "signed" event is not protected. Two Finish requests at the same moment (a double tap or a client retry) both succeed, because src/server/routes-sign.ts reads the recipient before waiting for the request body: the receiver gets two recipient.completed events with different ids, and a second "Signed" line is added to the audit trail after "Envelope completed". Declining twice at once gives two envelope.declined events and two emails to the sender (race.ts). No webhook test exists.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/envelopes.ts completeRecipient() and declineRecipient(): make the change conditional (UPDATE recipients SET status=... WHERE id=? AND status IN ('sent','viewed')) and return the first answer quietly when no row changed; read the recipient again inside the function instead of trusting the copy from find(). Build the event id from event, envelope and recipient so a repeat always carries the same id.

results.requirement: Every workspace can get viewed/signed/completed events by email digest or webhook without a native integration, and manual upload/download always works as a fallback.
results.evidence: Webhooks are open to every account with no plan check (src/server/routes-account.ts POST /webhooks; src/server/webhooks.ts): a free account with billing counted received envelope.sent, recipient.viewed, recipient.completed and envelope.completed, each signed correctly (hooks.ts). Emails per event are a per-user setting (notifyPrefs() and notifySender() in src/server/envelopes.ts; tests/trust.test.ts 'notifications are quiet by default and adjustable'). Upload, download and export have no plan or status gate (routes-envelopes.ts POST /files and GET /envelopes/:id/download; routes-trust.ts GET /export; tests/trust.test.ts 'everything can be exported...'); with sending paused and a zero balance all three still answered 200 (more.ts).
results.gap: Emails are one per event to the envelope's sender, not a digest, and only admins can set up webhooks.

results.requirement: Signed PDFs are standard flattened files whose signatures display in Adobe Acrobat, browser viewers and macOS Preview.
results.evidence: src/server/pdf.ts renderEnvelopePdf() flattens form fields in each source, paints signatures into the page as ordinary images and appends the certificate; there is no certificate-based signature that a viewer could fail to show. misc.ts: the result is an unencrypted PDF 1.7 with no form, its SHA-256 equals final_sha256 and /public/verify accepts it. I rendered a signed file with pdf.js (the engine in Firefox and in this app) and with poppler: signature, typed text and the flattened form values all show (tests/out/audit-developer/pdfjs-signed-form.pdf.png, form-p1-1.png).
results.gap: I could not open the files in Adobe Acrobat or macOS Preview here, and no test renders the output in any viewer. Two defects with real-world sources: a PDF with fillable fields comes out with page annotation entries that point at objects that no longer exist (poppler prints "Syntax Error: Invalid XRef entry"; strict checkers will reject the file), and an empty digital-signature field in the source survives as a live form widget (pdf.js lists Widget/Sig "Signature1") because a failing flatten() is swallowed by the try/catch.
results.suggested_fix: pdf.ts renderEnvelopePdf(): after flatten, remove from every page's /Annots each entry that does not resolve or whose Subtype is Widget, and drop /AcroForm; when flatten throws, remove the widgets field by field instead of carrying on. Add a test that signs a form PDF and asserts no Widget annotations, no dangling entries and a clean pdftoppm run. Before each release a person opens one signed file in Acrobat and in Preview.

bugs.title: Links in emails take their address from whoever made the latest request when APP_URL is not set
bugs.detail: baseUrl() falls back to one process-wide value that every request overwrites from its Host / X-Forwarded-Host header, and every tenant's emails use it. Reproduced with APP_URL unset (tests/out/audit-developer/misc.ts, more.ts): (1) POST /api/auth/forgot for a victim's address with header X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example produced a reset email whose link is https://evil.example/reset?token=<real token>. (2) One anonymous GET /api/me with that header, then the timer (cron tick), produced a reminder email to a signer whose button is https://evil.example/sign/<real signing token>: whoever runs evil.example can then sign as that person. The README says to set APP_URL in production but nothing enforces it. Fix: refuse to start in production without APP_URL, never take the address for emails from request headers, and pass the origin along with the request instead of keeping it in a global.

bugs.title: An Idempotency-Key returns another team member's envelope
bugs.detail: The replay path does loadEnvelope() on whatever the key maps to in the account, without the mine() check. Reproduced in api.ts: the owner creates an envelope with Idempotency-Key: contract-4471; a plain member (who gets 404 on GET /envelopes/<id>) posts anything with the same key and receives the owner's envelope with subject and recipient addresses. Keys such as an order or contract number are guessable. The same path also ignores a different body: a second, different request with a used key silently returns the first envelope. Fix: store user_id and a body hash with the key, run mine() on the replay, answer 409 on a mismatch.

bugs.title: An Idempotency-Key stops protecting once its first envelope has been deleted: every retry sends again
bugs.where: src/server/routes-envelopes.ts POST /envelopes; table idempotency_keys in src/server/db.ts
bugs.detail: The key row is written with INSERT OR IGNORE and never removed when the envelope is deleted. Reproduced in misc.ts: create a draft with key contract-4471, delete the draft, then create-and-send twice with the same key. Result: two different envelopes and two emails to the signer. The stale row points at nothing, so each call creates a new envelope and the new mapping is ignored. Fix: INSERT OR REPLACE when the old envelope is gone, or delete the row in DELETE /envelopes/:id.

bugs.title: Bulk send ignores Idempotency-Key and runs inside the request, so a timed-out call that is retried sends everything twice
bugs.detail: Reproduced in api.ts: the same POST /bulk twice with Idempotency-Key: bulk-1 created two batches and emailed each person twice (and holds twice the signatures when billing is on). The call sends up to 500 envelopes one after another and waits for the mail server on each, with no time limit of our own (100 rows took 0.46 s with no mail server at all; with a real one it grows by the mail server's response time per row), which is exactly when a client gives up and retries. Fix: honour the header on /bulk and return the first batch; queue the sends and return the batch id at once.

bugs.title: Failed webhook deliveries become impossible to send again because other customers' traffic erases them
bugs.where: src/server/webhooks.ts deliver() (the UPDATE that sets body=NULL); src/server/routes-account.ts GET /webhooks (LIMIT 30)
bugs.detail: Stored bodies are dropped for rows with id < MAX(id) - 200, but id is one counter shared by all accounts. Reproduced in more.ts: my webhook fails once (row can be resent), another account logs 250 deliveries, my next event arrives, and my one failed delivery now answers "This delivery is too old to send again." although I only ever had two deliveries. Also: the screen and GET /webhooks show only the latest 30 rows across all webhooks (45 failures in the log, 30 listed, no paging), and the log row is only written after all three tries, about six seconds after the event, so an event in flight during a restart leaves no trace (read from the code, not reproduced). Fix: count the 200 per webhook (ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 200), never drop the body of a failed delivery, add paging, insert the row before the first try.

bugs.title: Two Finish (or Decline) requests at the same moment are both accepted
bugs.where: src/server/routes-sign.ts POST /sign/:token/complete and /decline; src/server/envelopes.ts completeRecipient(), declineRecipient()
bugs.detail: The route loads the recipient, then waits for the request body, then acts on the stale copy. Reproduced in race.ts with Promise.all: both completes answer 200; the audit trail reads Signed, Envelope completed, Signed (the last line is added after the certificate was made, so the live trail no longer matches the certificate); the integration receives two recipient.completed webhooks with different ids. Two declines at once give two envelope.declined webhooks and two "Declined" emails to the sender. The signature ledger is not double-charged. Fix: conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ('sent','viewed') and stop when no row changed.

bugs.title: Removing a team member silently deletes their API keys and breaks whatever used them
bugs.detail: Reproduced in api.ts: a member's key works (200); the owner removes the member; the key answers 401 "Please sign in."; no email goes to anyone. The dialog says only that their documents are handed over. Admins cannot see other people's keys beforehand (GET /api-keys shows only your own), so they cannot know an integration depends on that person. Fix: list the keys in the dialog, hand them over or email admins which ones stopped, and return a 401 that says the key no longer exists.

bugs.title: An API key carries its creator's whole role, with no narrower permission
bugs.detail: A key made by an owner or admin can do everything that person can. Checked in misc.ts: with only the key, POST /account/invites {role:'admin'} answers 200 (the invited address then joins as an admin) and POST /api-keys mints further keys. By the same code path it can call transfer-owner, cancel the plan, trigger a refund and export every document. One leaked integration key is a full takeover of the account. Fix: key permissions (send-only, read-only, admin) and no team, billing or key management through a key unless it was created for that.

bugs.title: No webhook is sent when a signing link is replaced, so integrations keep handing out a dead link
bugs.detail: Reproduced in corr.ts: get a link with recipient-view; POST /envelopes/:id/correct with a new email. The old link answers 410 and zero webhooks are delivered. Same when the signer reassigns to someone else. Only PUT /envelopes/:id fires envelope.corrected. An integration that stored or is showing the old address has no signal to fetch the new one. Fix: fire envelope.corrected (with recipient_id and link_replaced) from both functions.

bugs.title: API keys keep working, and keep sending, after the account was closed
bugs.detail: Reproduced in closing.ts: POST /me/delete answers closed: 'scheduled' and signs the browser out, but the account's key still answers 200 and still sends a real envelope with a real email. Thirty days later the account, that envelope and its signing link are purged. Fix: delete or disable keys when closing_at is set (restore on sign-in), or refuse key requests while an account is closing.

bugs.title: Signed PDFs made from fillable forms contain broken annotation entries; empty digital-signature fields survive
bugs.detail: Reproduced in misc.ts and inspect.ts: upload a PDF with a text field and a checkbox, send, sign, download. The first page's /Annots has two entries pointing at objects that do not exist; pdftotext and pdftoppm print "Syntax Error: Invalid XRef entry 10 / 11". Display is fine in pdf.js and poppler, but strict validators and archive or filing systems can reject the file. With a source that has an unsigned signature field, the widget remains in the signed file (pdf.js reports Widget/Sig "Signature1"). Fix: strip unresolved and Widget entries from /Annots after flattening and do not swallow a failed flatten.

bugs.title: Every request for an embedded signing link adds a line to the audit trail and the certificate
bugs.detail: api.ts: 28 calls produced 28 "Signing link issued" audit rows, and the audit trail is printed in full on the certificate of completion. An integration that asks for the link on every page view will fill the certificate with pages of these lines. Fix: log once per recipient per day, or keep this event off the certificate.

bugs.title: Lower-case "bearer" is rejected as if no key was sent
bugs.detail: race.ts: Authorization: bearer <valid key> answers 401 "Please sign in." The scheme name is case-insensitive in HTTP and some clients send it in lower case; the answer gives no hint what is wrong. Fix: add the i flag and return a key-specific 401.

bugs.title: Webhook address check can be bypassed by a hostname that changes its answer (not reproduced)
bugs.detail: From reading the code: the hostname is resolved and checked, then fetch resolves it again, so a name that answers with a public address first and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 second gets a signed POST sent into the private network (the reply body is not returned, only the status is stored). The different messages "That hostname does not resolve" and "must point to a public address" also let an admin of any account probe internal names, and there is no limit on webhooks per account. Fix: connect to the address that was checked (custom lookup pinned to the validated IP), use one message, cap webhooks per account.

overclaims.where: src/server/webhooks.ts deliver(), email "A Sign&Grow webhook keeps failing"
overclaims.claim: "Nothing is lost: every event is kept in the delivery log, and once your side is fixed you can send each one again from Settings."
overclaims.reality: Settings lists only the latest 30 deliveries across all webhooks with no paging; stored bodies are dropped by a counter shared with every other account, so a failed delivery can answer "This delivery is too old to send again" after a single further event (reproduced); and an event whose three tries were still running when the server restarted is not in the log at all.

overclaims.where: src/server/openapi.ts, Idempotency-Key parameter on POST /envelopes
overclaims.claim: "Repeating a call with the same key returns the first envelope instead of creating another."
overclaims.reality: Once the first envelope has been deleted, every repeat with that key creates and sends a new envelope (reproduced: 2 envelopes, 2 emails). The first envelope is also returned to a different team member who is not allowed to see it, and POST /bulk does not honour the header at all.

overclaims.where: Settings, API and webhooks (src/app/app/settings/page.tsx) and WEBHOOK_EVENTS in src/server/webhooks.ts
overclaims.claim: "We POST JSON to your URL when an envelope is sent, opened, signed, corrected, completed, declined, voided or expires."
overclaims.reality: A correction made with POST /envelopes/:id/correct (the call for fixing one person's name, email or access code) sends no webhook, and neither does a signer reassigning to someone else, even though both can replace the signing link. Only a full PUT fires envelope.corrected (reproduced in corr.ts).

overclaims.where: src/server/openapi.ts info.description
overclaims.claim: "Errors are JSON: {\"error\": \"what went wrong and what to do\"}"
overclaims.reality: Every API key failure (missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, owner removed, lower-case "bearer") answers only "Please sign in.", which says neither what went wrong nor what a program should do.

overclaims.where: src/server/envelopes.ts sendEnvelope(), refusals 429 and 422
overclaims.claim: "New accounts can send to 50 people a day during their first week. Need more right now? Contact support." and "If it is genuine, use the contact form and a person will clear it for you."
overclaims.reality: The people running the service have no tool to do either for one account: the operator routes in src/server/routes-trust.ts can only pause or unpause an account and close requests and reports. The cap is one setting for every account, and an account that is free through GROWalition cannot lift it by paying because checkout is refused for it.
